critiques.assumption: Coordinator approval supplies reliable weekly membership cheaply.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 establishes heterogeneous schedules; their completeness and timing are explicitly unmeasured. A manifest could stabilize an incorrect set or move reconciliation work upstream. This vulnerability is supported; actual manifest failure is unobserved.
critiques.opening: Assess unresolved weekly intent before requiring routine manifest approval.
critiques.comparison: Z1 diagnoses metadata sensitivity; A1 pins membership. Adding explicit unresolved identity decisions tests whether pinning has a trustworthy input.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: compare coordinator decisions with independently specified fabricated weekly intent, including stale schedules and a split. Count incorrect approvals and all preparation minutes.

critiques.assumption: Correct membership and immediate regeneration provide additive handling savings.
critiques.limitation: Faster regeneration could repeat a wrong selection; conversely, fixing selection could remove replacement demand. Neither interaction is established by job durations or waiting times.
critiques.opening: Measure the combined mechanism against both individual changes before implementing both.
critiques.comparison: A1 reduces selection-related rework; A2 reduces request/return friction. Their interaction is potentially substitutive: reliable initial exports leave little regeneration work to accelerate.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: cross original/corrected membership with ordinary/simulated-immediate delivery; time active work separately from waiting.

openings.claim: A minimal weekly membership resolver exposes uncertain identities before a manifest is trusted.
openings.delta: Demonstrate one authorized course-week decision with provenance and an explicit unresolved split state.
openings.prediction: Explicit uncertainty prevents some incorrect approvals but may increase preparation time.
openings.probe: Proposed fabricated task; score decisions and total handling against supplied scenario intent.
openings.fit: conditional on existing or affordable stable identifiers and dated intent evidence; retain D1-C1–C4 and original success measures
assumptions: Missing dependencies can be assessed within six engineer-days; otherwise stop before implementation.

openings.claim: Pinned membership plus authorized regeneration helps only where residual replacement work remains.
openings.delta: Compare combined treatment with each parent and incumbent.
openings.prediction: Combination adds little when membership repair eliminates replacements; unresolved intent makes both ineffective.
openings.probe: Proposed four short fabricated conditions across two sessions per coordinator; record preparation, checking and request effort. No world tests performed.
openings.fit: preserves original outcome, next-40-export targets and D1-C1–C4
assumptions: Session capacity permits four brief tasks; simulated delivery cannot establish real interruption savings.
